original_value: Community policing to collaboratively maintain community safety and order in conjunction with law enforcement is becoming increasingly popular and efficient with the use of mobile technologies. Beyond sharing information about local problems such as crime via online discussion forums, there has been an increased focus on the impact of mobile crowdsourcing systems on community policing. In this study, we designed a novel crowdsourced patrolling campaign in which community members schedule their own patrol times and routes, then perform bike-based patrolling with video capturing using their smartphones. We conducted a four-week field study (n=20) on a university campus to verify the campaign's feasibility and observe users' behavior. Our results show key findings about users' task scheduling, event capturing and reporting behaviors, factors affecting task selection and execution and user motivation and engagement. Finally, we discuss several practical design implications in building crowdsourcing systems for community policing.

result.paraphrase: Community policing, which works with law enforcement to jointly maintain community safety and order, is gaining popularity and effectiveness through mobile technologies. In addition to sharing information about local issues such as crime in online forums, attention has increasingly turned to the effects of mobile crowdsourcing systems on community policing. In this study, we developed a new crowdsourced patrolling campaign where community members set their own patrol times and routes, then carry out bicycle patrols with video recording using their smartphones. We ran a four-week field study (n=20) on a university campus to assess the campaign’s feasibility and observe user behavior. Our results reveal key findings on users’ task scheduling, event capturing and reporting behaviors, factors influencing task choice and execution, and user motivation and engagement. Finally, we discuss several practical design implications for building crowdsourcing systems for community policing.
